_help: Drop any .docx, .html or .md file into content/sources (or .md into content/authored). It becomes a topic automatically. Add an entry here (keyed by file name) to set its title, emoji, colour and category.

genai-rag-agents.html.title: GenAI, RAG, Agents & Vector DBs
genai-rag-agents.html.subtitle: 225 interview questions in plain words, concepts, cheat sheets and code
genai-rag-agents.html.about: LLMs only know what they were trained on. RAG gives them an "open book": split your documents into chunks, turn them into embeddings, store them in a vector database, and fetch the closest passages for every question. Agents go further and let the model use tools in a loop. This topic covers all 225 interview questions in plain words.

voice-ai-agent.html.title: Voice AI Agents
voice-ai-agent.html.subtitle: STT → LLM + tools → TTS, latency, scenarios and working code
voice-ai-agent.html.about: A voice agent is a pipeline: speech-to-text (ears), an LLM with tools (brain and hands), and text-to-speech (mouth). The hard parts are speed (about 1 second to first audio), knowing when the user has finished talking, and handling mishearing safely. Stream every stage and confirm risky actions.

ai-engineer-fastapi-flask.docx.title: AI Engineer, FastAPI & Flask
ai-engineer-fastapi-flask.docx.subtitle: 69 interview answers with code and architecture diagrams
ai-engineer-fastapi-flask.docx.about: Real interview answers for AI Engineer roles plus Python web APIs. FastAPI is async, typed and validates input with Pydantic; Flask is small, synchronous and flexible. You will also find RAG system design, evaluation, and reports from real interviews.

react-node-interview.docx.title: React, Node.js & JavaScript
react-node-interview.docx.subtitle: HTTP, JS core, React, Express, TypeScript, Mongo, SQL, Redis, Docker
react-node-interview.docx.about: JavaScript runs your whole stack: React builds the UI from components and state, and Node.js runs JavaScript on the server with a non-blocking event loop. This guide covers HTTP, JS core, React, Express, TypeScript, MongoDB, SQL, Redis and Docker, with coding questions.

csharp-lessons.html.title: C# Lessons 1–99
csharp-lessons.html.subtitle: Every lesson explained line by line, with output to predict
csharp-lessons.html.about: C# is a typed, object-oriented language that runs on .NET. These 99 lessons go from Hello World and variables through loops, arrays, methods and classes to LINQ, async and dependency injection. Each lesson explains the code line by line; guess the output before you reveal it.

dotnet.md.about: .NET is the platform that runs C#: code compiles to IL and the CLR turns it into machine code. ASP.NET Core builds web APIs from three ideas: dependency injection, a middleware pipeline and configuration. EF Core maps your C# classes to database tables.

mongodb.md.about: MongoDB stores data as flexible JSON-like documents instead of rows. Data that is read together is stored together, so you embed or reference depending on how you query. Indexes keep reads fast, the aggregation pipeline transforms data in stages, and replica sets and sharding give availability and scale.

postgres.md.about: PostgreSQL is a relational database: tables, keys and SQL. It is famous for correctness (ACID transactions with MVCC), powerful indexes, and extras like JSONB and pgvector. Learn the order SQL runs in, joins, window functions, and how to read EXPLAIN to make queries fast.

agentic-langchain.md.about: An agent is an LLM in a loop: it thinks, calls a tool, reads the result and repeats until the job is done. LangChain gives you ready-made building blocks (models, prompts, tools, retrievers), and LangGraph lets you wire them into a graph with memory, branching and human approval. Learn when to use a simple workflow and when you really need an agent.

leetcode.md.about: LeetCode problems test a handful of patterns again and again: two pointers, fast/slow pointers, dummy heads, hash maps, sliding windows, stacks and binary search. Every problem here has a plain-English idea, a picture, a dry run, and solutions in both C# and JavaScript. Learn the pattern, not the answer.

leetcode-js.md.about: More coding-interview practice, all in modern JavaScript: hash maps, sliding windows, stacks, binary search, trees, graphs, dynamic programming, backtracking and heaps. It ends with Node.js tasks interviewers love (debounce, Promise.all, EventEmitter, retry, promise pool, streams). Learn the pattern first, then write the code yourself.

messaging.md.about: The big picture of messaging: queues, pub/sub and logs, which of Redis, MQTT or Kafka to pick, the delivery guarantees (at-most, at-least, exactly once) and the patterns every interview asks about (outbox, idempotent consumers, dead-letter queues, ordering), plus a capstone pipeline from sensors to Kafka.

redis.md.about: Redis is a very fast in-memory data store that also does messaging. Pub/Sub broadcasts live messages (nothing is kept), lists make a simple job queue, and Streams give you a durable log with consumer groups and acknowledgements. Follow the numbered tutorial in Node.js, run the commands in the browser console, then use the reference and quiz.

mqtt.md.about: MQTT is the lightweight publish/subscribe protocol for devices on weak networks. Clients publish to topics on a broker; wildcards (+ and #) let one subscriber listen to many devices. Learn QoS 0/1/2, retained messages, Last Will and persistent sessions in a step-by-step Node.js tutorial, with a wildcard tester and a QoS simulator.

kafka.md.about: Kafka is a durable, replayable log for events. Topics are split into partitions, messages with the same key stay in order, and consumer groups share the work. Follow the tutorial to create a topic, produce, consume, commit offsets, use acks and build a dead-letter topic, and play with partitions in the lab.

n8n.md.about: n8n is a workflow automation tool: connect nodes on a canvas so a trigger (webhook, schedule, app event) fetches data, transforms it and acts on it (Slack, email, CRM). Learn items, expressions, HTTP requests, branching, loops, error handling, AI agents and production set-up in 17 hands-on lessons, then practise the interview questions.

cicd.md.about: CI/CD means every code change is built, tested and released automatically. Learn GitHub Actions step by step (triggers, jobs, matrix, caching, artifacts, secrets, Docker, environments with approval), then release strategies (blue-green, canary, rollback), GitOps, security and the questions interviewers ask. Includes a pipeline simulator and a canary rollout lab.
